subject: Neighborhood And Urban Residential Zoning Proposal
overview: The Community Development Board hosted a public Q&A and information session to present the city's draft neighborhood and urban residential zoning proposal and collect community feedback.

items.title: Introduction and Overview of Zoning Project
items.summary: Zac Bears opened the meeting, followed by Planning Director Alicia Hunt and consultant Emily Innes, who explained the background of the zoning realignment process.

items.title: Proposed Residential Districts Presentation
items.summary: Emily Innes presented the specific density, housing types, and height limits proposed for the new Neighborhood Residential and Urban Residential districts.

items.title: Public Comments on Lower Hillside and Tufts Boundaries
items.summary: Laurel Ruma voiced concerns regarding the UR1 designation in the Lower Hillside, citing potential developer impacts on small lots and encroachment from Tufts University.

items.title: Housing Affordability and Wealth Accumulation
items.summary: Residents questioned the projected housing unit yield under the new zoning and emphasized the need for stable homeownership opportunities to build generational wealth.

items.title: Property Conversion Permitting Process
items.summary: Christian asked about the approval timeline for the new zoning proposal and the process for applying to add housing units under the draft code.

items.title: Lot Coverage, Green Space, and ADU Placement
items.summary: Cecilia Karlowitz and Mark Davidson requested details on open space requirements, lot coverage limits, and rules for upper-floor accessory dwelling units.

items.title: Density Distribution and Glenwood Development
items.summary: Cheryl Rodriguez objected to the zoning proposal, arguing that it disproportionately loads density onto small lots in Glenwood while larger-lot neighborhoods remain less dense.

items.title: Building Permits and Single-Family Rebuild Rules
items.summary: Christopher Dedic and Judith Weinstock sought clarification on the retroactive date of zoning advertisements and whether existing single-family homes in UR1 can be rebuilt.

items.title: NR1 Lot Sizes and Non-Conforming Additions
items.summary: Ren Bean advocated for lowering the lot minimums in the NR1 district to allow more two-family conversions and asked about grandfathering additions on non-conforming homes.

items.title: UR1 By-Right Single-Family Concerns
items.summary: Mike Korcynski criticized the removal of by-right single-family homes in the proposed UR1 district, urging for more permissive building rights.

items.title: Commercial Uses in Residential Zones
items.summary: Andrew MacRobert asked about integrating corner stores and neighborhood commercial hubs into the residential zones to support walkable neighborhoods.

items.title: Infrastructure and Traffic Concerns in Glenwood
items.summary: Carlene Campbell-Hegarty spoke in opposition to the UR1 and UR2 designations in her neighborhood, citing a lack of preparatory traffic, parking, and infrastructure studies.

items.title: Loophole Concerns, Height Restrictions, and Tree Canopy Protections
items.summary: Gaston Fiore, William Navarre, Anne Hegarty, and Laurie Krieger discussed potential density loopholes with multiple ADUs, building height limits, emergency vehicle access, and tree preservation.
